Only two terminals. n8 = MOSFET-P 3 gate: gate plate at y~438 (x 283-312), lead down at x~283 straight off the bottom edge; it meets I-AC 2 below the frame. Judgment calls: (a) The n3 horizontal crosses the x~272 column at (272,133) and the x~338 column at (338,135). BOTH crossings are drawn as a sharp V-notch dip in the horizontal (checked at 14x) - this drafter's crossover mark, NOT junction dots. Treating them as junctions would short MOSFET-P 5's gate to its own source (via x~338) and merge the whole bias column with the V-AC 6 drive line, which is electrically impossible, so both are read as hops. The only genuine dot on that band is the filled junction dot at (336,242). (b) MOSFET symbol reading: in every transistor here the long solid bar is the gate plate and its lead leaves from the plate's left end; the broken 3-segment bar is the channel; the middle channel stub carries the body arrow and is wired to one of the outer stubs - that outer stub is the SOURCE, the other is the DRAIN. MOSFETs 5, 10, 11, 14 are drawn gate-plate-up with the channel leads going down; MOSFETs 3 and 7 are drawn mirrored (channel leads up, gate plate below the channel). Body arrows point toward the channel on the N devices (10, 11, 14) and away from it on the P devices (3, 5, 7), matching the given classes. This body-tie reading also agrees with the 'drain toward the supply, source toward ground' heuristic for every device: M10 S=0/D=n4, M7 S=0/D=n6, M11 S=n4/D=n5, M14 S=n5/D=n2, M5 S=n5/D=n2, M3 S=n6/D=n5. (c) OFF-FRAME COMPONENTS (bbox centres outside the 512x512 crop, symbols not in the image): V-AC 4 at (177.7,-51.9) and Zener Diode 9 at (353.4,-47.2) sit above the top edge; I-AC 2 at (165.1,571.9) sits below the bottom edge. Exactly three wires leave the top edge - x~88 (the ground rail), x~272 (n1) and x~418 (n2) - and exactly two leave the bottom edge - x~101 (the ground rail) and x~282 (n8). V-AC 4 spans x 155-201, i.e. between the x~88 and x~272 exits, so it is read as bridging 0 and n1. Zener 9 spans x 337-370, i.e. between the x~272 and x~418 exits, so it is read as bridging n1 and n2. That pairing is the only one that leaves no open end anywhere and it makes the circuit function: the zener sits from the +5V rail down to the bias column that drives the gates of MOSFET 5 and MOSFET 11, with V-AC 4 returning that column to ground. I-AC 2 spans x 142-188, between the x~101 and x~282 bottom exits, so it is read as bridging 0 and n8 (it is the gate drive for MOSFET-P 3, exactly mirroring I-AC 0 which drives MOSFET-P 7's gate). (d) 2-terminal order is as drawn (left/top first); for V-DC 1 index 0 is the '+' plate (top, to n2) and index 1 the '-' plate (bottom, to GND 13).
